GRU4Rec’s max losses normalize over negatives using softmax weights: BPR-max is −log Σⱼwⱼσ(r₊−rⱼ), plus λΣⱼwⱼrⱼ²; TOP1-max weights its ranking and score-shrinkage terms similarly. Do not add another division by negative count. Sampled cross-entropy instead normalizes over the positive and sampled candidates; its logQ correction depends on the sampling distribution. Official GRU4Rec shares other batch targets as negatives and adds samples proportional to item frequency raised to sample_alpha. Consequently, restricting which positions contribute batch targets can change negative count, popularity distribution, duplicates and loss difficulty—even with identical supervised positives. [Paper](https://hidasi.eu/assets/pdf/gru4rec_v2_cikm18.pdf), [official implementation](https://github.com/hidasib/GRU4Rec/blob/master/gru4rec.py).

Experimental-design implication: suffix supervision should use Σmℓ/Σm, with padding excluded, and apply the same retained-position reduction to score regularization. Averaging masked zeros over the original tensor changes gradient scale and regularization balance. A matched full-context versus cropped-context ablation must hold fixed exact target positions, minibatch membership/order, candidate IDs and multiplicities, accidental-positive filtering, sampling probabilities/corrections, loss and regularization coefficients, initialization, optimizer, update count, schedule, clipping and evaluation. Precompute or explicitly pair negative pools; identical seeds alone do not ensure identical draws when execution changes. Change only the history available before each retained target. Full-context prefix states must remain connected to suffix losses; detaching them introduces a gradient-horizon intervention. Handle left padding without recurrent state updates and read the final nonpadding position. Matching retained targets alone therefore does not establish an isolated context intervention; these controls follow from the objectives and sampler above.
